**Best Majors for Law School Preparation (Texas Tech Online)**

Texas Tech University Online offers several majors that are excellent preparation for law school. Law schools do not require a specific undergraduate major, but they value strong skills in critical thinking, writing, research, and analysis. Here are some recommended majors you can pursue online at Texas Tech if you plan to attend law school:

---

**Recommended Online Majors for Law School:**

- **Legal Studies (B.A. or B.A.A.S.)**
  - Specifically designed for students interested in law or legal careers.
  - Emphasizes legal theory, critical thinking, legal research, writing, and hands-on experiences like internships and mock trials.
  - [B.A. in Legal Studies Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=17360&hl=Legal+Studies%2C+B.A.+%E2%80%93+Online%2B&returnto=search)
  - [B.A.A.S. in Legal Studies Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=20534&hl=Legal+Studies%2C+B.A.+%E2%80%93+Online%2B&returnto=search)

- **English (B.A.)**
  - Develops advanced reading, writing, and analytical skills.
  - Strong foundation for the reading- and writing-intensive nature of law school.
  - [English, B.A. – Online Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=20500&hl=English%2C+B.A.+%E2%80%93+Online&returnto=search)

- **Political Science (B.A.)**
  - Focuses on government, policy, and legal systems.
  - Builds understanding of the political context of law.
  - [Political Science, B.A. – Online Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=20503&hl=Plant+and+Soil+Science%2C+B.S.%3A+Horticulture+Concentration+%E2%80%93+Online&returnto=search)

- **History (B.A.)**
  - Emphasizes research, argumentation, and understanding of legal and social change.
  - [History, B.A. – Online Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=18425)

- **Criminology (B.A.)**
  - Focuses on criminal law, justice systems, and sociological aspects of law.
  - [Criminology, B.A. – Online Degree Details](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=17224&hl=Criminology%2C+B.A.+-+Online&returnto=search)

- **Philosophy, Sociology, or Communication Studies**
  - These majors also build skills in logic, argumentation, and communication—valuable for law school.

---

**Additional Tips:**
- Law schools value high academic achievement and strong skills over any particular major.
- Choose a major that interests you and allows you to excel academically.
- Consider adding a minor in Legal Studies, Political Science, English, or Writing to further strengthen your law school application.

Glossary

$10K Degree Completion Program. Texas Tech's pathway for adults who already have college credit and want to finish a bachelor's degree. "10K" means a target cost of about $10,000 for students who qualify. It is not a financial filing. You may also see it written as 10K or 10-K. Two degrees are available: a Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies and a Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies. If you qualify, you could finish for as little as $10,000. Your advisor will estimate your cost, because it depends on the credit you already have.

Applicable credit hours. College credit that counts toward this degree, not every credit you have earned. With at least 80 applicable credit hours, including your core courses, you could finish for as little as $10,000. With 70 to 79, you can still enroll. Your advisor will tell you which of your credits apply.

Core curriculum (core courses). The general-education courses you need before you can finish a bachelor's degree. This program expects those courses to be complete before you start.

Asynchronous. Coursework you complete on your own schedule. It is not a live class at a set time. After the microcredentials, the rest of the degree is taught this way.

Hybrid. A mix of online work and in-person class. In this program, the microcredentials are online, with in-person meetings two Saturdays a month at Texas Tech DFW or Texas Tech El Paso. You can choose a morning session (9 AM–12 PM) or an afternoon session (1 PM–4 PM).

Microcredential. A free 4-week course led by Texas Tech faculty. This program has four required courses. You can take them in any order, and textbooks are included. If you complete them, you can turn them into 12 credit hours toward your degree. Each course also comes with a digital badge.

Digital badge. An online record that shows you finished a microcredential. You earn one for each course.

Glossary

Digital badge. An online record that shows you finished a microcredential. You earn one for each course.

Prior learning credit. Credit for work or life experience, not for a college class. An advisor helps you build a prior learning portfolio. This program can award up to 9 credit hours this way. Together with the microcredentials, that can be up to 21 credit hours before you pay to convert them.

Flat program fee. One set price, not a charge for each credit hour, to turn completed microcredentials and prior learning into official credit toward your degree. The microcredential classes themselves are free. This fee is what converts that work, and eligible prior learning, into degree credit.

Concentration. A focused set of courses in one subject. In the Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies, you choose three.

Non-traditional learner. An adult returning to college, often while working, rather than a recent high-school graduate attending full time. This program is built for you.

Glossary

$10K Degree Completion Program. Texas Tech's pathway for adults who already have college credit and want to finish a bachelor's degree. Core curriculum (core courses). The general-education courses you need before you can finish a bachelor's degree. This program expects those courses to be complete before you start.
